descriptionChirho: The noun denoting a price, cost, or monetary value paid for something, used in contexts of buying land, purchasing items, or figuratively the cost of wisdom. All four clusters represent the same noun with different prepositions (be- 'for', construct 'price of') and pronominal suffixes ('its price', 'their price'). Arabic consistently uses thaman (ثَمَن) across all clusters, Spanish 'precio' (price) throughout, Hindi 'daam/mulya' (दाम/मूल्य, price/value), Korean 'gabs' (값, price/cost), and Swahili 'bei' (price) uniformly. These are inflectional variants (absolute, construct, with suffixes, with prepositions) of a single lexical sense.
